metadata.title: GEEK Protocol — Kaspa Basics Gauntlet (DRAFT)
metadata.schema: correctIndex is zero-based; options contains four distinct strings
metadata.reviewNotice: Draft, practice-only and unranked: every row has practiceOnly true, is excluded from ranked, daily, lobby, duel and royale selection, and is not counted as source-checked. 10 rounds x 10 (round-N tags): easy rounds 1-3, medium 4-7, hard 8-10. Facts still need owner/editorial review before any status change.

questions.prompt: Kaspa's ledger is structured as a what?
questions.funFact: Kaspa keeps parallel blocks in a directed acyclic graph instead of a single chain.

questions.prompt: Who earns newly minted KAS?
questions.funFact: Block rewards go to proof-of-work miners; Kaspa has no staking.

questions.prompt: Which way do Kaspa block links point?
questions.funFact: Each new block references earlier blocks as parents.

questions.prompt: In a DAG, what does 'acyclic' mean?
options: Every block links to all others
questions.funFact: Following parent links never returns to the starting block.

questions.prompt: How were Kaspa's first coins distributed?
questions.funFact: Kaspa launched with no premine, insider allocation or presale.

questions.prompt: What happens to parallel blocks in Kaspa?
questions.funFact: Kaspa merges parallel blocks rather than discarding them as orphans.

questions.prompt: Besides Hebrew University, Kaspa research continued at?
questions.funFact: Kaspa's lore traces its research to the Hebrew University and later Harvard.

questions.prompt: What kind of product is KasWare?
questions.funFact: KasWare is a Kaspa wallet that dApps reach through window.kasware.

questions.prompt: KRC-20 is a Kaspa standard for what?
questions.funFact: KRC-20 defines deploy, mint and transfer operations for fungible tokens.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare event fires when the balance changes?
questions.funFact: Listen for balanceChanged to refresh displayed funds.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method changes the wallet's network?
questions.funFact: switchNetwork asks the wallet to move to another Kaspa network.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method ends a dApp's connection?
questions.funFact: disconnect removes the site's wallet connection.

questions.prompt: KRC-20 tokens live on which network?
questions.funFact: KRC-20 operations ride on ordinary Kaspa transactions.

questions.prompt: How does a Kaspa block identify its parents?
questions.funFact: Headers list parent block hashes.

questions.prompt: How many parents can a Kaspa block reference?
questions.funFact: Kaspa blocks reference multiple parent tips, merging parallel work.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method returns the account's public key?
questions.funFact: getPublicKey returns the public key, never the private key.

questions.prompt: Which protocol defines the KRC-20 standard?
questions.funFact: KRC-20 operations are processed by the Kasplex indexer.

questions.prompt: GHOSTDAG colors blocks blue or what?
questions.funFact: Well-connected blocks are blue; the rest are red.

questions.prompt: Kaspa's research began at which university?
questions.funFact: Kaspa grew out of blockDAG research at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

questions.prompt: In Kaspa, what does BPS stand for?
questions.funFact: Mainnet targets 10 BPS.

questions.prompt: What does a KRC-20 'tick' field hold?
questions.funFact: The indexer validates and uppercases the tick.

questions.prompt: What does a higher block rate mainly cut?
questions.funFact: More frequent blocks mean transactions are included sooner.

questions.prompt: What do KRC-20 transfers pay network fees in?
questions.funFact: Every KRC-20 operation is a Kaspa transaction paying KAS fees.

questions.prompt: A KasWare signMessage signature proves control of?
questions.funFact: Signing a message proves key control without moving funds.

questions.prompt: Which KRC-20 operation destroys tokens?
questions.funFact: The burn operation removes units from a holder's balance.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method asks the user to connect?
questions.funFact: Call requestAccounts only after a user action, such as a click.

questions.prompt: What do Kaspa miners race to find?
questions.funFact: A block is valid when its kHeavyHash result meets the target.

questions.prompt: Which upgrade came right before Toccata?
questions.funFact: Crescendo (2025) preceded Toccata (2026).

questions.prompt: What is Kaspa's emission schedule called?
questions.funFact: Rewards fall smoothly each month, halving every year.

questions.prompt: Kaspa's DAA score is used in place of?
questions.funFact: In a DAG there is no single height, so a DAA score orders time.

questions.prompt: How often do Kaspa block rewards step down?
questions.funFact: Each month the reward drops by a factor of (1/2)^(1/12).

questions.prompt: Chromatic halving cuts emission by how much per year?
questions.funFact: Twelve monthly steps combine into one halving per year.

questions.prompt: Each monthly reward step multiplies by what?
questions.funFact: That ratio mirrors one semitone on a tempered scale.

questions.prompt: GHOSTDAG's k at 10 BPS is set to?
questions.funFact: k scales with block rate; at 1 BPS it was 18.

questions.prompt: In what year was the PHANTOM paper first posted?
questions.funFact: It appeared as IACR ePrint 2018/104.

questions.prompt: Max parents per block at 10 BPS?
questions.funFact: Rusty Kaspa caps parents at 16 to bound processing.

questions.prompt: How does Kaspa choose a block's selected parent?
questions.funFact: The parent with the highest accumulated blue work is selected.

questions.prompt: Linked selected parents form which chain?
questions.funFact: Kaspa's ordering follows the selected parent chain back from the virtual block.

questions.prompt: What does Kaspa's 'virtual' block represent?
options: A view over all DAG tips
questions.funFact: The virtual block merges current tips to define the node's state.

questions.prompt: How long must a KRC-20 ticker be?
questions.funFact: Ticker validation rejects names shorter than 4 or longer than 6.

questions.prompt: Minimum indexer fee to deploy a KRC-20 token?
questions.funFact: Deploys below 1,000 KAS fail with 'fee not enough'; rules may change.

questions.prompt: Minimum indexer fee per KRC-20 mint?
questions.funFact: Each mint must pay at least 1 KAS; rules may change.

questions.prompt: Which KRC-20 deploy field sets the amount per mint?
questions.funFact: lim is the amount each mint receives.

questions.prompt: Which KRC-20 deploy field caps total supply?
questions.funFact: Mints stop once minted supply reaches max.

questions.prompt: Which KRC-20 deploy field pre-allocates supply?
questions.funFact: pre credits tokens to the deploy's to address.

questions.prompt: Default KRC-20 decimals when dec is omitted?
questions.funFact: Validation fills a missing dec with 8.

questions.prompt: Which KRC-20 operation offers tokens for sale?
questions.funFact: The Kasplex list operation moves the amount from the seller's balance to locked and records a market order.

questions.prompt: Who computes KRC-20 token balances?
questions.funFact: Kaspa nodes do not track KRC-20; the Kasplex indexer derives balances.

questions.prompt: How is KRC-20 data placed on Kaspa?
questions.funFact: Wallets build a commit then a reveal transaction carrying the operation.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method reads the active network?
questions.funFact: getNetwork is read-only and needs no approval.

questions.prompt: What does KasWare's getNetwork return on mainnet?
questions.funFact: Testnet 10 returns kaspa_testnet_10.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method sends KAS to an address?
questions.funFact: sendKaspa builds and sends a native KAS payment.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method signs a text message?
questions.funFact: signMessage proves address control without spending.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare event fires on an account switch?
questions.funFact: dApps listen for accountsChanged to refresh the address.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare event follows a fee-bump replacement?
questions.funFact: KasWare emits transactionReplacementResponse after a replacement attempt.

questions.prompt: When should a dApp call KasWare's requestAccounts?
questions.funFact: KasWare's docs say never to request a connection on page load.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare call reads already-connected accounts?
questions.funFact: getAccounts returns the connected current account address (an array) and is used to check whether the site is connected.

questions.prompt: In PSKT, what does the 'T' stand for?
questions.funFact: PSKT means partially signed Kaspa transaction.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method signs a PSKT?
questions.funFact: signPskt signs; pushPskt broadcasts.

questions.prompt: At mainnet's 10 BPS, coinbase outputs mature after how many blocks?
questions.funFact: Rusty Kaspa sets coinbase maturity to BPS x 100 seconds, so 10 BPS gives 1,000 blocks (about 100 seconds).

questions.prompt: Kaspa's minimum relay fee is quoted per what mass unit?
questions.funFact: The baseline is 1 sompi per gram of transaction mass.

questions.prompt: How long did Kaspa's pre-chromatic phase last?
questions.funFact: It ran from November 2021 to May 2022.

questions.prompt: Blocks a block newly adds to its past form its?
questions.funFact: The mergeset is what a block merges beyond its selected parent's past.

questions.prompt: What does a block's blue score count?
options: All the blocks in its past
questions.funFact: Blue score grows with the blue blocks a block inherits.

questions.prompt: GHOSTDAG treats blue blocks as what?
questions.funFact: Blocks published promptly by honest miners tend to be blue.

questions.prompt: In 'DAA score', what does DAA stand for?
questions.funFact: DAA score is a monotonic counter used in place of block height.

questions.prompt: Which KIP specified the Crescendo hardfork?
questions.funFact: KIP-14 bundled KIP-9, 10, 13 and 15.

questions.prompt: What did Kaspa's Toccata upgrade add?
questions.funFact: Toccata brought covenants and ZK verification to layer 1.

questions.prompt: What reward mix did Kaspa's first two weeks use?
questions.funFact: The random-reward subphase averaged about 750 KAS per block.

questions.prompt: A KRC-20 mint after max supply is reached is?
questions.funFact: The KAS transaction confirms, but the indexer credits no tokens.

questions.prompt: A ticker submitted as 'kasp' is stored as?
questions.funFact: Ticker validation uppercases the tick.

questions.prompt: Besides deploy, which KRC-20 op has a minimum fee?
questions.funFact: Transfer, burn and list have no minimum indexer fee.

questions.prompt: Which characters may a KRC-20 ticker use?
questions.funFact: Each tick character must fall in A-Z after uppercasing.

questions.prompt: A KRC-20 'issue'-mode deploy is keyed by?
questions.funFact: Issue mode sets the tick to the deploy transaction ID.

questions.prompt: How does the indexer treat a transfer from a blacklisted holder?
questions.funFact: The transfer check fails when the sender is blacklisted for that token.

questions.prompt: In PHANTOM, k mainly reflects what?
questions.funFact: k is chosen so honest blocks rarely exceed k in each other's anticone.

questions.prompt: Why is GHOSTDAG called greedy?
options: It inherits the selected parent's coloring
questions.funFact: Each block extends its selected parent's blue set instead of solving globally.

questions.prompt: Finding PHANTOM's exact max k-cluster is?
questions.funFact: That hardness motivated the greedy GHOSTDAG approximation.

questions.prompt: What does pruning keep intact?
questions.funFact: Pruned nodes still hold full spendable state.

questions.prompt: How do Kaspa nodes drop old block data?
questions.funFact: Pruning discards old block bodies to bound storage.

questions.prompt: Which proposal makes Kaspa's k adapt to latency?
questions.funFact: DAGKnight (KIP-2) is still proposed; details may change.

questions.prompt: What did SPECTRE lack that PHANTOM added?
questions.funFact: SPECTRE ordered pairs of blocks, which suits payments but not smart contracts.

questions.prompt: Before chromatic halving, KAS was minted at what rate?
questions.funFact: The pre-deflationary phase ran until May 2022.

questions.prompt: What rate did chromatic emission start at?
questions.funFact: 440 matches the frequency of the note A4.

questions.prompt: The 440 starting rate echoes which musical note?
questions.funFact: Each monthly step is a semitone; each year is an octave.

questions.prompt: In which year did the chromatic phase begin?
questions.funFact: The pre-deflationary phase ended on May 8, 2022.

questions.prompt: What does getNetwork return on Testnet 10?
questions.funFact: Network names may change as testnets are replaced.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method returns spendable UTXOs?
questions.funFact: getUtxoEntries returns the account's UTXO entries.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare call broadcasts a signed PSKT?
questions.funFact: Sign with signPskt, then broadcast with pushPskt.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare call builds a KRC-20 inscription script?
questions.funFact: buildScript prepares the script for KRC-20 commit-reveal.

questions.prompt: kHeavyHash wraps its matrix step in which hash?
questions.funFact: Rusty Kaspa's PoW hashers are cSHAKE256 instances.

questions.prompt: Kaspa's emission is fixed per what unit?
questions.funFact: Raising BPS splits the same per-second subsidy across more blocks.

questions.prompt: Kaspa addresses sign with which default scheme?
questions.funFact: Standard Kaspa addresses use Schnorr public keys.

questions.prompt: Who co-authored the GHOSTDAG paper with Sompolinsky and Zohar?
questions.funFact: The paper is 'PHANTOM and GHOSTDAG: A Scalable Generalization of Nakamoto Consensus' (IACR ePrint 2018/104).

questions.prompt: Where do a deploy's pre-allocated tokens go?
questions.funFact: The indexer verifies the to address before crediting pre.

questions.prompt: A deploy reusing an existing ticker is?
questions.funFact: Each tick can be deployed only once.

questions.prompt: Error for a deploy paying under 1,000 KAS?
questions.funFact: 'fee unknown' applies when no fee is detected.

questions.prompt: About when will KAS rewards fall below 1 sompi?
questions.funFact: The wiki's 1-BPS estimate counts from mainnet start.

questions.prompt: What caps how many blocks one block may merge?
questions.funFact: Mergesets over the limit make a block invalid.

questions.prompt: Which KasWare method signs a KRC-20 transaction?
questions.funFact: KasWare's KRC-20 API pairs buildScript with signing helpers.
